input.question: What design or KIP describes how to route older clients without rack information to same-rack replicas?

content.content: {"result":"{\"answer\":\"**Direct answer:**  \\nThe design is described in **KIP-1150 (Diskless Topics)**, in its cluster metadata section, which specifies that for older clients without rack information, the broker can encode the rack information in the client ID and \\\"lie\\\" to the consumer by replacing the leader with one of the replicas from the same rack if available.\\n\\n**Supporting facts in time order:**  \\n- 2026-01-23T12:01:44.000000Z - In message `mail:dd72e188e244a14eeb227fa2`, Ivan Yurchenko states: if the MetadataRequest is of the new version and contains RackId, the broker tells the truth (real leader, replicas, preferred produce brokers, IsDiskless flag) and lets the client decide; if the MetadataRequest is older (no RackId), older clients continue to work but cannot benefit from inter-rack traffic elimination. As a workaround, the rack information can be encoded in the client ID, in which case the broker \\\"lies\\\" to the consumer by replacing the leader with one of the replicas from the same rack if available. This is part of the KIP-1150 Diskless Topics design (the cluster metadata section added to the KIP wiki).
